skill.name: gsap-animations
skill.description: Guidance for implementing GSAP animations with scroll triggers, performance safeguards, accessibility support, responsive behavior, and visual QA workflows.
skill.summary: Build accessible, performant GSAP animations for WordPress and web projects.
skill.author: CrazySwami

security_audit.summary: Static findings for shell execution, screen capture upload, and system reconnaissance are false positives caused by Markdown examples and checklist wording. The hardcoded URLs are public GSAP CDN and documentation references, not hidden network behavior. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found, but the front matter grants broader tool permissions than the guidance usually needs.

remediation.suggestion: Limit allowed tools to the minimum needed, such as Read and Edit, and remove Bash unless a documented workflow requires it.
When recommending CDN scripts, add guidance for trusted sources, version pinning, and Subresource Integrity where possible.

content.value_statement: Complex scroll animations can hurt performance and accessibility. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through GSAP setup, patterns, testing, and cleanup.
actual_capabilities: Explains GSAP setup through CDN and WordPress enqueue examples.
Provides fade, stagger, parallax, reveal, curtain, and hero timeline patterns.
Recommends reduced-motion handling and CSS fallbacks.
Outlines responsive matchMedia behavior and ScrollTrigger refresh practices.
Shows visual QA and Playwright screenshot timing practices.
Includes reusable animation library patterns and a launch checklist.
limitations: It provides guidance and snippets, but it does not install GSAP by itself.
Examples assume browser JavaScript and WordPress where relevant.
Some advanced GSAP plugins may require separate GreenSock licensing.
Performance still depends on page weight, assets, devices, and implementation quality.

use_cases.title: Add Scroll Animations
use_cases.description: Plan and implement scroll-triggered reveals, parallax, and staggered content without hiding essential content.

use_cases.title: Review Animation Performance
use_cases.description: Check whether animations use transform and opacity, avoid layout thrashing, and clean up unused ScrollTriggers.

use_cases.title: Prepare Visual QA
use_cases.description: Make animated pages easier to screenshot by completing, skipping, or stabilizing animation states during tests.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Reveal
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a small page section.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the gsap-animations skill to create an accessible fade-in reveal for this section. Respect reduced motion and keep content visible without JavaScript.

prompt_templates.title: Improve ScrollTrigger Timing
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my ScrollTrigger animation plan with the gsap-animations skill. Suggest better start points, cleanup behavior, and mobile-safe defaults.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Animation Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the gsap-animations skill to audit this page for layout thrashing, excessive triggers, reduced-motion gaps, and screenshot stability issues.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Reusable System
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the gsap-animations skill to design a reusable GSAP animation system for cards, hero sections, parallax media, and visual QA workflows.

output_examples.input: I need scroll reveals for cards on a WordPress landing page.
output_examples.output: A plan that enqueues GSAP and ScrollTrigger, reveals cards with staggered opacity and transform, and includes reduced-motion fallbacks.

output_examples.input: My page animation feels slow and affects layout.
output_examples.output: A review that flags layout properties, recommends transform and opacity changes, and adds cleanup for unused ScrollTriggers.

output_examples.input: Our screenshots catch animations halfway through.
output_examples.output: A testing approach that completes animations before screenshots or skips them through a stable query parameter.

best_practices: Respect reduced-motion preferences before starting nonessential animations.
Animate transform and opacity instead of layout properties.
Refresh and clean up ScrollTriggers when content or routes change.
anti_patterns: Do not hide essential content until JavaScript runs.
Do not leave ScrollTrigger markers enabled in production.
Do not use complex pinned animations on mobile without testing real devices.

faq.question: Does this skill install GSAP?
faq.answer: No. It explains setup patterns and snippets that a developer can apply in a project.

faq.question: Can it help with WordPress themes?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a WordPress enqueue example for GSAP, ScrollTrigger, and theme animation scripts.

faq.question: Does it cover accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It emphasizes reduced motion, visible content without JavaScript, and avoiding critical content behind animations.

faq.question: Does it include testing guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers visual QA, Playwright screenshots, and stable animation states for screenshots.

faq.question: Can it replace performance testing?
faq.answer: No. It provides best practices, but teams still need to test real pages on target devices.

faq.question: Are paid GSAP plugins required?
faq.answer: No for most examples. Some optional plugins mentioned by the skill may require separate licensing.
